## formal
Assume the hypothesis of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy} (the counted units carry the entropy $A/4$, the area-law hypothesis), with the arrays of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} version 3, weights $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$, each carrying $\tfrac12\ln 2$ at the Hawking temperature (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}), sixteen per generation per light ray (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}). A \emph{grouping} assigns each array to one registered unit; let $\bar u$ be the mean number of arrays per unit.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(No premise fixes the grouping; proved.)} Every premise of the cone holds for every grouping: they constrain modes, arrays, their weights and states, and the density of (C2) (Premise \claimref{singularity.c2-cell-density}, which leaves $\nu$ free), and none mentions how arrays are grouped. J3 (\claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction}) partitions the modes into $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ channels and, with (Q) version 3, puts one array in each helicity channel; it supplies a candidate grouping (units as channels, or as the two helicity channels of one $(\omega, \ell, m)$, the choice \claimref{synthesis.capacity-per-mode-independent-of-helicity}(iii) records J3 as deciding) but no premise identifies a registered unit with a channel or a pair of channels, so the grouping stays free. Reading the density $\nu$ of (C2), which counts fermionic modes per Planck cell with one ladder pair per point, as a density of registered units of arrays is the framing of the problem, not (C2)'s literal text. The models differ in the residue, $\kappa_{c} = 1/(2\bar u\ln 2)$, and in $\nu$ by the same factor.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(What the residue requires; proved.)} The registered residue $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\ln 2)$ holds exactly when $\bar u = 2$: on average two arrays per unit, eight units per generation, whatever the sizes of the individual units (of the $231$ groupings of a generation's sixteen arrays by size, exactly the $22$ with eight units qualify; uniform units qualify only at two arrays). No smaller structural unit qualifies: a boundary mode is one ladder pair of capacity $\ln 2$ (\claimref{synthesis.capacity-per-mode-independent-of-helicity}), and at these weights every mode has $|x| \ge \pi$, where $s(\pi) < 0.21 < \ln 2$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}). At the offset $0$ an array carries more than $\ln 2$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}(ii)), so no union of whole arrays averages $\ln 2$ there; only the zero-weight mode does, with the rest of its array outside the count.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Light rays are not registered units.)} With $c$ arrays per light ray, the light rays per Planck area per modular period are $1/(2c\ln 2)$, independent of the grouping, and on the cosmological horizon, under (R$_{\Lambda}$) with the same weights and $S = \pi N^{2}$ (\claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}), they number $2\pi N^{2}/(c\ln 2)$; the registered units number $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$ exactly at $\bar u = 2$, which is $c/2$ units per light ray: $8n_{g}$ for the fermion content, which is $c$ under J3's reading of the integer-weight channels as currents of the arrays, $24$ at three generations. The count $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$ is therefore that of registered units, not of light rays as \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number} words it (its argument uses only that $N$ is common, which stands).
\end{enumerate}
So the residue does not fix the count unit; it requires its mean to be two arrays, an input recorded by decision, and the registered density $\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$ of \claimref{pred.boundary-mode-density} rests on that input.

## technical
Under the area-law hypothesis the residue is one over four times the mean entropy per counted unit. Each array of (Q) version 3 carries exactly half of $\ln 2$ at the Hawking temperature, so the residue takes its registered value exactly when the counted units hold two arrays on average, eight per generation of sixteen Weyl components; units of unequal size with that mean do equally well, and a uniform unit must be a pair. Nothing in the premises says how arrays are grouped, and the cell-density premise leaves the density free, so every grouping gives a model of the premises with its own residue: the unit is a recorded input. The literal structural unit, one ladder pair, cannot carry the capacity at these weights, since no mode has zero weight; at the other offset an array carries more than $\ln 2$, so no union of arrays fits there. The light rays are fewer than the registered units: their number is fixed by the area law and the number $c$ of arrays per light ray, $2\pi N^{2}/(c\ln 2)$ on the cosmological horizon, which is $c/2$ times fewer than the $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$ registered units, twenty-four times fewer for three generations of fermions.

## lay
The series predicts how densely a black hole's horizon is packed with the elementary carriers of its entropy, and that prediction depends on what counts as one carrier. The natural building blocks each carry exactly half a bit's worth of entropy, so the prediction comes out right only if a carrier is, on average, two blocks. This result shows that nothing in the theory's assumptions decides how blocks are grouped into carriers: every grouping is consistent, and only the average of two gives the predicted density. It also corrects a count: the number of light rays on the universe's horizon is smaller than the number of carriers, by a factor set by how many blocks each light ray holds, twenty-four for the known three generations of matter particles.

## one-liner
Under the area law the residue $1/(4\ln 2)$ holds exactly when the counted units average two arrays of (Q) version 3 (eight per generation, any unit sizes); no premise fixes the grouping, no single ladder pair qualifies, and the light rays number $2\pi N^{2}/(c\ln 2)$, $c/2$ times fewer than the registered units.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Setting.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(i), under its hypothesis $\sum_{j \in J}s_{j} = A/4$ over the counted units $J$, the residue is $\kappa_{c} = |J|/A = 1/(4\langle s\rangle)$ with $\langle s\rangle$ the mean entropy per unit. In the quasi-free state the entropy of a set of arrays is the sum of their entropies, and at the weights of (Q) version 3 each array carries exactly $\tfrac12\ln 2$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}(i), given the imported theta-function identities). A unit of $u_{j}$ whole arrays therefore carries $\tfrac12u_{j}\ln 2$, and $\langle s\rangle = \tfrac12\bar u\ln 2$ with $\bar u = |J|^{-1}\sum_{j}u_{j}$.

(i) \emph{Premise by premise.} (P), (R), (R$_{\Lambda}$) and (Q) fix the marginals, the joint quasi-free KMS state and the weights of the modes of each array; (N$_{+}$) and the window reading (\claimref{synthesis.window-reading-array-killing-energy}) fix the null ground state and read each array as one chiral component of a light ray on one window; (C1) and (C3) place the modes and fix the counted epoch; (C2) (\claimref{singularity.c2-cell-density}) fixes the form of the density and leaves $\nu$ free; (IC) fixes the clock; J3 identifies channels with two-dimensional modes; the slot-module hypothesis and the results built on it fix the content, sixteen Weyl components per generation per light ray (\claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}); J3 (\claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction}) identifies each $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ channel with a two-dimensional mode, and with (Q) version 3, whose consequence clause reads one array as one helicity channel, it partitions the arrays into channels; \claimref{synthesis.capacity-per-mode-independent-of-helicity}(iii) records that what J3 decides is how ladder pairs group into channels, so whether the horizon's entropy is matched by one or two helicity channels per $(\omega, \ell, m)$. That is a candidate grouping, not a definition of the registered unit: no premise says that a registered unit is a channel or a pair of channels, so J3 holds for every grouping. (C2) counts fermionic modes per Planck cell, one ladder pair per point of the blown-up boundary; reading its $\nu$ as a density of registered units made of arrays is the problem's framing, and under it every value of $\nu$ is admitted. The other postulates of the cone at the pinned versions, P1 to P5, R1 to R3, H1, T14's (U) on rank-one eigenvalues, the interface premise (I), the rate inputs (L, U), the common-ceiling premise (the reversal pair), the indifference premise and tameness, concern towers, couplings, channel occupancies, the boundary-mode dynamics and constructions; the foundation, tower and imported statements concern algebras and representations; none mentions a grouping of arrays. Each is a statement about modes, arrays, their weights and states, or about content, and none mentions a partition of the arrays into registered units, so a regrouping, which changes nothing they mention, carries a model of all of them to a model of all of them. The models differ in $|J|$ at fixed area and fixed array count, so in $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\langle s\rangle) = 1/(2\bar u\ln 2)$, and in the registered density, which is proportional to $\kappa_{c}$ (\claimref{pred.boundary-mode-density}); (C2) admits every value.

(ii) $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\ln 2)$ if and only if $\langle s\rangle = \ln 2$, that is $\bar u = 2$. Per generation, a grouping of the sixteen arrays into $k$ units has $\bar u = 16/k$, so it qualifies exactly when $k = 8$, whatever the unit sizes; the check runs over the $231$ integer partitions of $16$ (groupings up to which arrays go where) and finds the $22$ with eight parts, among them the all-pairs grouping and $(9, 1, \dots, 1)$; for uniform units $1/(2u\ln 2) = 1/(4\ln 2)$ only at $u = 2$. \emph{Ladder pairs.} A boundary mode is one ladder pair, of capacity $\ln 2$ (\claimref{synthesis.capacity-per-mode-independent-of-helicity}); a mode of weight $\omega$ has entropy $s(x) = \ln(1 + e^{-x}) + x/(e^{x} + 1)$, $x = 2\pi\omega/\kappa$, even and decreasing in $|x|$, with $s(0) = \ln 2$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}). At the weights $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$, $|x| = |2k + 1|\pi \ge \pi$, and with $u = e^{-x}$, $s \le u + xu$; since $e^{3} > (1 + 1 + \tfrac12 + \tfrac16 + \tfrac1{24} + \tfrac1{120})^{3} > 20$ and $\pi > 3$, $e^{-\pi} < \tfrac1{20}$, so $s(\pi) < (1 + \tfrac{16}{5})/20 = \tfrac{21}{100}$, while $\ln 2 = \sum_{k \ge 1}1/(k2^{k}) > \tfrac{69}{100}$ (partial sums). No single ladder pair carries $\ln 2$; a unit carrying it must contain modes of several arrays, and among unions of whole arrays only the mean of two does. \emph{Offset $0$.} There an array carries $S_{0} = \ln 2 + 2\sum_{k \ge 1}s(2\pi k) \in (0.72039, 0.72040)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}(ii)), above $\ln 2$, so any union of $u \ge 1$ whole arrays carries more than $\ln 2$; only the zero-weight mode carries exactly $\ln 2$, leaving $S_{0} - \ln 2$ of its array outside the count, the case of \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(vi).

(iii) Under the hypothesis at a horizon of area $A$ the arrays carry $A/4$, so there are $A/(2\ln 2)$ arrays per modular period whatever the grouping (\claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}(iii)); with $c$ arrays per light ray there are $A/(2c\ln 2)$ light rays. On the cosmological horizon the same computation applies under (R$_{\Lambda}$) with weights $\kappa_{\Lambda}(k + \tfrac12)$, the entropy of an array depending only on $x = 2\pi\omega/\kappa_{\Lambda}$; with $A/4 = \pi N^{2}$ (\claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}), the arrays number $2\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, the light rays $2\pi N^{2}/(c\ln 2)$ and the registered units $2\pi N^{2}/(\bar u\ln 2)$, which is $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$ exactly at $\bar u = 2$. Units per light ray are $c/\bar u = c/2$; for the fermion content $c = 16n_{g}$, so $8n_{g}$, which is $24$ at $n_{g} = 3$; under J3 (\claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction}), which reads the integer-weight channels as currents of the arrays, the bosons add no arrays and $c = 16n_{g}$; a reading that adds boson null data as further arrays would raise $c$. The note of \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number} calls $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$ a count of light rays, citing the boundary-mode count of Observation \claimref{standard-model.largeness-number-universes-boundary-modes}; by the above it is the count of registered units, and the light rays are $c/2$ times fewer. That proof uses only that the count is common to the towers, which holds for both, so its conclusions stand.

check_py:
"""Exact checks: what the calibration residue requires of the count unit, and what it leaves free.

Arrays are those of (Q) version 3 (weights kappa(k + 1/2)), sixteen per generation per light ray (the Weyl
components). Entropies are kept as rational multiples of ln 2 where the stored results give them exactly
(an array carries (1/2) ln 2, the zero-weight mode ln 2) and bracketed by rationals otherwise
(s(pi) from e^(-pi) < e^(-3) < 1/20, ln 2 from partial sums of sum 1/(k 2^k)). A grouping of the sixteen
arrays of a generation into k units is an integer partition of 16 into k parts; the registered residue under
the area-law hypothesis is kappa_c = 1/(4 <s>), and in units of 1/ln 2 it is k/(4 * 8) per array-half.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

ARRAYS_PER_GENERATION = 16
HALF = F(1, 2)          # an array's entropy in units of ln 2 at the Hawking temperature (stored, exact)


def partitions(n, largest=None):
    largest = n if largest is None else largest
    if n == 0:
        yield ()
        return
    for first in range(min(n, largest), 0, -1):
        for rest in partitions(n - first, first):
            yield (first,) + rest


def ln2_bounds(N):
    lo = sum((F(1, k * 2 ** k) for k in range(1, N + 1)), F(0))
    return lo, lo + F(1, (N + 1) * 2 ** N)


def check_mean_two_arrays_is_what_the_residue_requires():
    """Over all 231 groupings of a generation's sixteen arrays, mean unit entropy equals ln 2 (so
    kappa_c = 1/(4 ln 2) under the area-law hypothesis) exactly for the 8-unit groupings, the mean being two
    arrays per unit whatever the part sizes; the all-pairs grouping is one of 22 such."""
    premise("synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2")
    premise("synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy")
    premise("synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components")
    allp = list(partitions(ARRAYS_PER_GENERATION))
    assert len(allp) == 231
    hits = []
    for p in allp:
        k = len(p)
        mean_s = F(ARRAYS_PER_GENERATION, k) * HALF      # in units of ln 2
        kappa_c = 1 / (4 * mean_s)                         # in units of 1/ln 2
        if kappa_c == F(1, 4):
            hits.append(p)
            assert F(sum(p), k) == 2
        else:
            assert F(sum(p), k) != 2
    assert len(hits) == 22 and (2,) * 8 in hits and (9, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1) in hits
    # uniform units of u arrays: kappa_c = 1/(2u) in units of 1/ln 2, the registered value only at u = 2
    assert [u for u in range(1, 17) if 1 / (4 * u * HALF) == F(1, 4)] == [2]
    GA.check("the residue requires a mean of two arrays per unit, eight units per generation", True)


def check_no_single_ladder_pair_and_no_zero_offset_union_carries_ln2():
    """At the weights kappa(k + 1/2) every mode has |x| >= pi, and s(x) <= (1 + x) e^(-x) gives
    s(pi) < 21/100 < 69/100 < ln 2: no single ladder pair carries the capacity. At the offset 0 an array
    carries ln 2 + epsilon > ln 2, so no union of whole arrays averages ln 2 per unit there (u S_0 > ln 2)."""
    premise("synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy")
    premise("synthesis.capacity-per-mode-independent-of-helicity")
    pi_hi = F(16, 5)
    u_hi = F(1, 20)                       # e^(-pi) < e^(-3) < 1/20 since e^3 > 20
    e_lo = sum((F(1, f) for f in (1, 1, 2, 6, 24, 120)), F(0))
    assert e_lo ** 3 > 20
    s_pi_hi = (1 + pi_hi) * u_hi
    assert s_pi_hi == F(21, 100)
    lo, hi = ln2_bounds(12)
    assert lo > F(69, 100) and hi < F(70, 100)
    assert s_pi_hi < lo
    # offset 0: S_0 = ln 2 + 2 sum_{k>=1} s(2 pi k) > ln 2; the stored bracket starts at 0.72039
    s0_lo = F(72039, 100000)
    assert s0_lo > hi
    for u in range(1, 9):
        assert u * s0_lo > hi
    GA.check("no ladder pair at the half offset, and no array union at offset 0, carries ln 2", True)


def check_light_rays_are_arrays_over_content_not_registered_units():
    """Under the area-law hypothesis arrays per Planck area per period are 1/(2 ln 2) (stored); with c arrays
    per light ray the light rays per Planck area are 1/(2 c ln 2), independent of the unit, and on the de Sitter
    horizon (area 4 pi N^2) they number 2 pi N^2/(c ln 2); registered units number pi N^2/ln 2 only at two
    arrays per unit, so registered units per light ray are c/2: 8 n_g for the fermion content, 24 at n_g = 3."""
    premise("synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components")
    premise("synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared")
    premise("dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number")
    arrays_per_area = F(1, 2)            # in units of 1/ln 2
    area = 4                              # de Sitter horizon area in units of pi N^2
    entropy = 1                           # pi N^2
    assert arrays_per_area * area * HALF == entropy * F(1, 1)
    for n_g in (1, 2, 3, 4):
        c = ARRAYS_PER_GENERATION * n_g
        for u in (1, 2, 4):
            rays = arrays_per_area * area / c          # light rays, in units of pi N^2 / ln 2
            units = arrays_per_area * area / u         # registered units, same units
            assert rays == F(2, c) and units == F(2, u)
            assert units / rays == F(c, u)
        assert F(c, 2) == 8 * n_g
    assert F(ARRAYS_PER_GENERATION * 3, 2) == 24
    GA.check("light rays = 2 pi N^2/(c ln 2); registered units per light ray = c/2", True)


EXPORTS = {"partitions": partitions}
